cards.title: Today’s vocabulary
sections: raincoat · /ˈreɪnkoʊt/ · noun · Word · New
a coat made to keep rain off your body. Puck has a raincoat but no umbrella.
hood · /hʊd/ · noun · Word · New
the part of a coat that can cover your head. Pull up your hood in the rain.
keep dry · /ˌkip ˈdraɪ/ · verb phrase · Phrase · New
to stay dry or prevent something from getting wet. Keep your phone dry in a closed bag.
in the rain · /ɪn ðə ˈreɪn/ · prepositional phrase · Phrase · New
outside while rain is falling. We walk home in the rain.
under cover · /ˌʌndɚ ˈkʌvɚ/ · prepositional phrase · Phrase · New
in a place with a roof or shelter above you. Wait under cover until the rain stops.

articulation.label: umbrella
articulation.alt: umbrella: /ʌ/ → /m/ → /b/ → /r/ → /ɛ/ → /l/ → /ə/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
/b/: Close lips briefly; release into the next vowel.
/r/: Bunch the tongue; leave space at the ridge.
/ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/l/: Tip at the ridge; air passes round the sides.
/ə/: Relax the tongue in the center.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Read and write
sections: Reading

Heart and Puck walk home in the rain. Heart's raincoat has a hood, so her head stays dry. Puck has no coat. They wait under cover by a shop until the rain becomes lighter. Heart keeps their paper tickets dry inside her bag.
Find the answer
Why do they wait by the shop, and how does Heart protect the tickets?
Write
Write two sentences using two words from today’s new word bank.
